subject: INITIALIZE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB416.md LANDED -- both halves of SR4 are now screened, by the two rules the standard's two paragraphs name. The SET half (the five §14.9.20.4 GR4 categories) was already CheckInitializeReplacingSetCategoryAgrees/COBOL1983; the MOVE half is CheckReplacingMoveValidity/COBOL2031, asked once per REPLACING item over the category-name SET. Because the rule's receiving operand is 'an item of the specified category' and not any item identifier-1 contains, the screen is a pure bind-time test of each (category, sender) pair and walks no receivers. The question is asked of MoveTable16 -- the SAME screen MoveBinder asks -- so the implicit MOVE and the explicit one cannot disagree; InitializeCategories.Table16Receiver maps a category-name to its Table-16 receiving position and a drift test asserts that EVERY category-name is screened by exactly one of SR4's two paragraphs, so the fourteenth word cannot arrive unscreened. The whole category-keyed validity question is covered, not the table alone: §14.9.25.3 SR1's sending half (SenderClassRefusal), SR8, SR7, SR6 (ShapeRefusal) and SR10 (Refusal). RESIDUE, stated: §14.9.25.3 SR5's figurative-to-numeric prohibition is an EDITION row living in VersionConformancePass.GateMove, re-derived from a bound MOVE node INITIALIZE never builds, so 'INITIALIZE g REPLACING NUMERIC DATA BY SPACE' is still un-gated at 2023 where 'MOVE SPACE TO n' is COBOL0902 -- the version lane's own row, reported rather than copied here edition-blind.
